**Test image observations:**
- Multiple soybean leaves showing uniform brown/orange/tan discoloration
- Leaves appear leathery and dying, drying out
- Petioles remain attached while leaves are dying
- Stems appear still green/healthy
- Pods visible and appear normal/green
- No obvious spots or lesions — broad, diffuse leaf browning

**Reasoning:**
- The test image shows leaves with a bronze/orange-brown discoloration across large portions of the leaf surface — consistent with Cercospora blight, which causes "leathery and dark purple with bronze highlights" coloration
- The widespread upper-surface discoloration and severe defoliation pattern (leaves dying while petioles remain) matches Cercospora's key diagnostic feature: "severe disease can cause defoliation while petioles remain attached"
- Cercospora reference shows dark purple blotching progressing to bronze/leathery leaves — the test image appears to show a more advanced stage of this
- Sudden Death Syndrome was considered, but SDS typically shows interveinal chlorosis with veins remaining green — not visible here
- Brown Stem Rot was considered but requires internal browning of stem pith
